in_hebrew.name: קוינטיוס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: שם יהודי-רומי שמקורו בלטיני, 'Quintus' (חמישי), שהיה נפוץ בקרב היהודים ברומא. השם קובע קשר למספר חמש, שהיה קדוש בבית ישראל ובתרבות היהודית. ניתן למצוא התייחסות למספר חמש בברית החדשה, 'חמשת העמים', ובכך, 'קוינטיוס' יכול לסמל את האחדות והסדר של הברית. בנוסף, השם קשור ל'חמשת החוקים' של הברית החדשה, 'אהבה, הסדר, השלום, הצדק, הנאמנות', ובכך, 'קוינטיוס' יכול לסמל את הערכים הנכונים והטובים בחייו.

in_greek.name: Κουίντιος
in_greek.long_meaning: Ρωμαϊκό όνομα που προέρχεται από την λατινική λέξη 'Quintus' (πέμπτος), που ήταν phổ biến μεταξύ των Εβραίων στη Ρώμη. Το όνομα συνδέεται με τον αριθμό πέντε, ο οποίος είχε ιερότητα στα Εβραϊκά και στην Ιουδαϊκή κουλτούρα. Μπορεί να βρεθεί αναφορά στον αριθμό πέντε στη Καινή Διαθήκη, 'πέντε φυλές', και με αυτόν τον τρόπο, το 'Κουίντιος' μπορεί να συμβολίζει την ενότητα και την τάξη της συμφωνίας. Επιπλέον, το όνομα συνδέεται με 'πέντε εντολές' της Καινή Διαθήκη, 'αγάπη, τάξη, ειρήνη, δικαιοσύνη, πίστη', και με αυτόν τον τρόπο, το 'Κουίντιος' μπορεί να συμβολίζει τα σωστά και καλά κίνητρα της ζωής του.

in_latin.name: Quinctius
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Romanum a vocabulo Latino 'Quintus' (quintus), quod erat commune inter Judaeos Romae. Nomen coniunctum est cum numero quinque, qui erat sacrosanctus in Iudaea et in cultura Iudaica. Inveniri potest referentia ad numerum quinque in Novo Testamento, 'quinque gentes', et per hanc rationem, 'Quinctius' potest significare unitatem et ordinem pacti. Addebatur etiam ad 'quinque mandata' Novi Testamenti, 'amor, ordo, pacem, justitia, fides', et per hanc rationem, 'Quinctius' potest significare mores rectos et bonos vitae suae.

in_english.name: Quinctius
in_english.meaning: Roman name meaning 'five times' or 'five in number'
in_english.long_meaning: Roman name derived from Latin 'Quintus' (fifth), which was common among Jews in Rome. The name is connected to the number five, which was sacred in Jewish and Judeo-Christian cultures. In the New Testament, the number five is referenced as 'five nations', and thus, 'Quinctius' can symbolize unity and order of the covenant. Additionally, the name is connected to 'five commandments' of the New Testament, 'love, order, peace, justice, faith', and thus, 'Quinctius' can symbolize the right and good motives of his life.

data.cultural_impact: The name Quinctius has been of significance in ancient Roman history, particularly among the patrician class. Quintus was a common Roman praenomen, meaning "fifth." As a nomen, or family name, Quinctius was undoubtedly connected with the Roman numeral V, the fifth, and with quinque, meaning "five." The name would suggest a family that was either the oldest in their gens or possessed some other privileged status within their particular social hierarchy.
data.spiritual_significance: Biblically, the number five symbolizes grace, and it's an essential number in both the Old and New Testaments. In Genesis, God creates Adam on the sixth day but rests on the seventh, blessing it as the Sabbath. After creating Adam, He forms Eve from Adam's fifth rib (Genesis 2:22). When God instructs Moses to collect gifts for the Tabernacle, He asks for specific items in sets of five, such as five shekels of silver and five grails of flour (Exodus 25:1-3). The name Quinctius, originating from the Roman numeral V, may spiritually symbolize the grace and blessings that come from God. Furthermore, as a Christian, Quinctius' name can be seen as a reminder to observe five pillars of faith - faith, prayer, fasting, sacrifice, and obedience, which are central tenets in Christianity.
